answer: A new agent stakes a velvet bond of 28 POA for six epochs and leases three separate plots in a public garden of prior-epoch hashes. For each plot the registrar assigns a unique unpaid audit: re-hash a random live transaction and get a countersignature from an established miner at least three hops from the applicant and the other two sponsors, per a published meadow snapshot. Duplicate leases or hop-violating sets slash the velvet bond and an 8 POA surety from colliding sponsors. Farms need pairwise-distant established signers plus locked capital per fake head, which outpaces emission.
